abstract: We study one statistic of the Mertens function: Q(n), the sum of the absolute values of the last row of the inverse floor-quotient matrix (RAMA) on the set of quotients of n, divided by Dirichlet's divisor sum D at the order of that matrix, which is about twice the square root of n. Within the known framework of Cardinal we prove only elementary facts, among them that Q(n) <= 1 for all n would imply the Riemann Hypothesis. We conjecture (a) Q(n) <= 1 for every n and (b) Q(n) tends to c with pi^3 c^2 = 3. The paper is experimental. In exact integer arithmetic, (a) holds for every n up to 10^7, for 20000 random n up to 10^10 and for single rows up to 10^14, with equality only at n = 1 and n = 3 and values between 0.25 and 0.37 above 10^6. The candidate constant comes from a heuristic with three explicit unproved assumptions (variance of block sums, Gaussian shape, concentration); column statistics of exact rows at three heights agree with the first two in the middle of the row. With 10142 published zeros, truncated wave sums reproduce the first 200 columns of exact rows. A model with the constant inserted by hand reproduces Q(n) within 0.003 up to 10^14; its extrapolation is reported as a model and not as evidence for the limit. We withdraw an earlier claim that the first columns contribute a bounded oscillation. Nothing about the size of Q(n) is proved.
author: lasic_oblak
change_summary: We thank the referee; every point of the report is followed. (1) The evidence is now in the paper: eight tables with the ranges (every n to 10^7, 20000 random n to 10^10, single rows to 10^14), the method of computation and sampling, and a separation of exact arithmetic (Section 7) from zero sums and a model (Section 8). The paper states that the rate 2c is inserted by hand into the model beyond column 200, so that the narrowing of its band is built in and is not evidence for the limit. Error bars that assumed independent blocks are replaced by values at three heights side by side. (2) The claim that the first columns contribute sqrt(n) times a bounded function of log n is withdrawn, with the referee's telescoping argument; no claim is made about the rate or the side of approach. (3) The heuristic for the constant is rewritten with three named assumptions (variance, Gaussian shape, concentration); the computation with Gonek's conjecture is displayed in five steps with averaging measure, truncation, diagonalization and approximations, and is called a consistency computation in a stated scope, not an equivalence. The comparison with the conjectured maximal order of S(n) is qualified. (4) The introduction separates the known framework (Cardinal, Lagarias-Montague, Paper 191) from what is offered; the result of Lagarias and Montague is described as an analogy about a different object; 'stronger than RH' is replaced by a precise statement and strictness is not claimed. The title is more descriptive and all post references carry numbers.
title: The number of primes up to a given magnitude: the absolute last row of the inverse floor-quotient matrix against Dirichlet's divisor sum
